review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: There is an opinion that news media caused many problems on people's lives today and this is a negative development. From my perspective, I agree that news media bring many impacts to people's lives but this is a both negative and positive development.

I strongly believe that news media have a lots influence on our lives. Firstly, the innovation of smartphones and the development of Internet allow people to follow the news instantly whenever and wherever they are, making news become a regular part of their routine. Secondly, the intense competition among news outlets in order to gain attention also lead to many effect for people. Most media agencies focus on shocking and breaking content and present it in a highly sensationalized manner with dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals, which reinforces the overall impact of news on public opinion.

Admittedly, news media is a negative trend since it can makes people feel overly anxious and helpless because of the exposure to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news even in situations that do not directly affect them. However, we shouldn't deny the benefit of news on people's lives. The coverage of news can warn the public to existing and looming problems in society, say, crime, natural disasters or political corruption. This helps individuals has better informed and more prepared each to respond to potential threat or even handle risks in an increasingly complex society.
In conclusion, Despite the influence of news media, I believe that this development brings both positive and negative.

Tuy nhiên, câu đầu đổi nghĩa đề thành gây vấn đề; câu chủ đề Body 2 chỉ gọi truyền thông là tiêu cực dù đoạn có cả lợi. Các lỗi a lots, can makes, helps individuals has và kết bài thiếu danh từ cho thấy em cần tự soát cấu trúc câu kỹ hơn. Cô giữ chuỗi ý và cách giải thích riêng của em, sửa đúng những điểm làm nghĩa hoặc câu chưa hoàn chỉnh.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Some people believe that the development of advertising has positive economic impacts. Others think it can cause negative social effects because it will make people dissatisfied with who they are and what they have. From my perspective, there are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

Admittedly, some people who advocate the development of advertising might argue that it can create many positive impacts for economy. Since creative content and appealing visual effect can simulate consumer demand, meaning that buying power and production are on the increase. This naturally follows that there are more employment opportunities and greater state revenues through taxation, which lead to a stronger economy. For example, in Vietnam, Shopee or Lazada rely heavily on advertising campaigns to attract customers, boosting not only their sales but also the entire digital retail sector. Moreover, advertising creates many jobs in marketing, media and design, thus can make it become an important driver of economic activity.

However, many users believe that advertising has negative social consequences. Because advertising constantly show images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards or luxury possession, it can foster dissatisfaction among viewers. Say, young people, in particular, often feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadget advertised on TikTok or Facebook, leading to frustration when they cannot afford them. Added to this, advertising promote materialistic values and a money-driven culture in the long run, which can cause many consequences for social.
Overall, I think that both views are valid to some certain extent. Advertising can contribute to social dissatisfaction and it also play a crucial role in economic development.

paragraphs: Some people believe that advertising generates positive economic effects, whereas others argue that it can create social dissatisfaction. There are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

On the one hand, supporters of advertising often point to the undeniable economic benefits it can bring. Creative content and appealing visual effects can stimulate consumer demand, meaning that spending power and production increase. This naturally results in more employment opportunities and greater state revenues through taxation, which lead to a stronger economy. For example, Shopee and Lazada in Vietnam rely heavily on advertising campaigns to attract customers, boosting both their sales and the digital retail sector. Furthermore, advertising creates jobs in marketing, media, and design, making it an important driver of economic activity.

Those on the other side of the debate, however, argue that advertising entails negative social consequences. Advertisements constantly show images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards, and luxury possessions, fostering dissatisfaction among viewers. Young people in particular may feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadgets advertised on TikTok or Facebook, leading to frustration when they cannot afford them. In addition, advertising promotes materialistic values and a money-driven culture in the long run.
In conclusion, I believe both views are valid to a certain extent. Advertising can contribute to social dissatisfaction while also playing a crucial role in economic development.

paragraphs: Some people believe that only students who show the best academic result will be rewarded by their school, while others argue that it is more essential to reward students who show improvement. Personally, I think that both groups of students deserve to reward.

Admittedly, it is undeniable that students who have the best performance need to be reward. Since students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve to praise and privilege for it. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards and also propel towards overall academic gains in the future. Moreover, this kind of competition is seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded. Thus students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition and it is enable for them to achieve success in later life.

However, I strongly believe that school also needs to reward students who show improvement. If only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, others might think that their efforts is futile because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals. This leads to prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened so students gradually lose the incentive to study. By emphasizing improvement, school can encouraged all students to be diligent in their studies and help them to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves regardless of how well they have been or are performing. This might teach them that the constant desire to outdo themselves even benefit themselves more than the competition determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that students who show the best performance and others who show improvement should be rewarded by their school.

Chuỗi ở Body 2 từ 'efforts is futile' đến 'lose the incentive to study' có hướng lập luận đúng. Tuy nhiên, các khung 'deserve to reward', 'deserve to praise and privilege', 'This leads to prone to feeling' cho thấy em ghép động từ và tính từ chưa kiểm soát; Body 1 còn dùng 'it is enable for them'. Mức vận dụng nội dung đạt nhưng độ chính xác ngôn ngữ yếu. Em cần viết lại các câu đó, tự xác định chức năng từng từ rồi đối chiếu bản chữa. paragraphs: Some people believe that schools should reward students who show the best academic results, while others argue that it is more essential to reward students who show improvement. Personally, I think that both groups of students deserve to be rewarded.

Admittedly, it is undeniable that students who have the best performance need to be rewarded. Firstly, since students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve their praises and privileges for this effort. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, thereby contributing to overall academic gains. Moreover, this kind of competition is seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded. Thus, students become used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition. This can enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, I strongly believe that schools also need to reward students who show improvement. To begin with, if only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, others might think that their efforts are futile. This is because they feel unable to surpass those outstanding individuals. This may leave these students feeling overwhelmed and disheartened. As a result, they may gradually lose the incentive to study. By emphasizing improvement, schools can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help them to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves regardless of how well they have been or are performing. This might teach them that the constant desire to outdo themselves may even benefit them more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that students who show the best performance and others who show improvement should be rewarded by their school.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Nowadays in some countries, children are being taught by their parents at home instead of by teachers at school. Although such development is beneficial to certain extent, I believe that the disadvantages that it offers are far more pronounced.

People who support homeschooling may argue that it allows parents to save money because no school fees are required. Home educated children are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, which may cause emotional and mental problems. When parents teaching their children at home by themselves, it can be easy for them to tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones. This is often not the case in traditional schooling because of the large class size.

However, this educational approach does not actually save money since parents need to pay a large amount of money for lab equipment and tutors while one parent may need to be cut off to cater for their child's needs, be these academic or personal. Besides that, most parents are not well-versed in all school subjects so it can be difficult for them to properly explain concepts to children and ultimately leading to academic problems. Moreover, even social problems that children may be faced with at school, say bullying and having romantic feeling for others, can prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.

In conclusion, although it is true that homeschooling may bring about a few advantages, these are relatively minor and should not overshadow the far more significant and long-lasting drawbacks it entails.
review.overall: Em viết đủ bốn đoạn, giữ lập trường hại hơn từ mở đến kết và bao quát cả sáu nhánh dàn ý. Body 1 chưa có câu chủ đề riêng để quy ba lợi ích về người ủng hộ; em đi thẳng từ 'People who support...' vào tiền học. 'When parents teaching' và 'ultimately leading' còn sai cấu trúc. Em cần thêm câu khái quát và sửa chuỗi nguyên nhân–hệ quả, tránh chỉ xếp ý theo thứ tự.

paragraphs: Nowadays, in some countries, children are being taught by their parents at home instead of by teachers at school. Although this approach is beneficial to a certain extent, I believe that the disadvantages that it offers are far more pronounced.

People who support homeschooling may argue that it offers several benefits to parents and children. Initially, it allows parents to save money as no school fees are required. In addition, home-educated children are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, which may cause emotional and mental problems. Finally, when parents teach their children at home themselves, they can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones. This is often not the case in traditional schooling owing to the large class size.

However, these benefits may be outweighed by significant costs and developmental drawbacks. Initially, this approach may not actually save money, since parents need to pay for lab equipment and tutors; one parent may also need to set aside working time to cater for the child's academic or personal needs. Besides that, most parents are not well versed in all school subjects; therefore, they may struggle to explain concepts to children properly, which can lead to academic problems. Moreover, even social problems that children face at school, such as bullying and having romantic feelings for others, can prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, although homeschooling may bring a few advantages, these are relatively minor and should not overshadow the far more significant and long-lasting drawbacks it entails.
